newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains vs spot dlr, dips in forwards.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains vs spot dlr, dips in forwards.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained against the spot dollar on Thursday but lost ground in the forward dollar market, dealers said.
"There is paying pressure," said a forward dealer.
He said some banks were covering ahead for Haj pilgrims's dollar requirements in the first quarter of calendar 1997.
Banks which had built up large forward commitments were also downsizing in view of the recent spurt in domestic call money rates, some dealers said.
Six month premium closed at 1.71/73 rupees on Thursday, off the day's high of 1.73/76 rupees and up from the opening level of 1.67/70 rupees, dealers said.
Premia for near term dollars also rose correspondingly.
One dealer said the recent volatility which saw the rupee dip to a low of 35.84 earlier this month had triggered some interest in forward cover among some Indian firms.
The spot dollar closed at 35.6950/7000 rupees, down from the opening level of 35.70/72, dealers said. Most of the day's deals were at 35.71, with a few deals at below the 35.70 mark.
